articles.title: New monolithic ion trap opens quantum simulations to more researchers
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Some quantum systems are so complex that even the most powerful supercomputers struggle to simulate their behavior. One solution is quantum simulation: building a controllable quantum system in the lab and tuning it to mimic the one researchers want to understand.

articles.title: A new way to detect stabilizing properties of optical devices
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: In optical fibers, chips and other light-guiding devices, minor defects can scatter photons and disrupt their path. A new study demonstrates a way to reveal properties which, in certain systems, help light wave behavior withstand such flaws. The method could help speed up the search for new kinds of electronics and optical technologies, and contribute to more reliable quantum devices.

articles.title: Physicists prove a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Whether we are waiting for a car windshield to defrost in winter or a warm drink to cool down, how long it takes for an object to settle into a stable, even temperature within its environment (thermal equilibrium) depends on numerous factors. These can include surface area, the material properties of an object and airflow.

articles.title: Physicists create a bizarre new quantum state called a fractional fermi sea
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered a strange new state of quantum matter in which ultracold atoms defy familiar organizational rules, forming a highly excited yet surprisingly orderly configuration called a "fractional Fermi sea." The discovery challenges established quantum theories and hints at exotic quasiparticles that scientists have dubbed potential "super-Fermions."

articles.title: Black Death had dramatic effect on species diversity as humans abandoned farmland, study finds
articles.summary: Researchers have found that during the Black Death, when a third of the population of Europe was wiped out, biodiversity fell. Understanding their farming practices could help us increase diversity in modern agriculture.

articles.title: Magic mushroom ingredient takes the fight out of aggressive fish
articles.summary: A psychedelic compound found in magic mushrooms appears to have an unexpected effect: calming highly aggressive fish. Researchers discovered that low doses of psilocybin significantly reduced aggressive attacks in mangrove rivulus fish without disrupting their normal social interactions. The findings suggest psilocybin may selectively calm escalating aggression rather than simply suppressing all behavior.
